question: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & x & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & x \\ x & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$. For what value(s) of $x$ is $A$ singular?
explanation:
$|A| = 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & x \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} - x \begin{vmatrix}1 & x \\ x & 1\end{vmatrix} + 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ x & 1\end{vmatrix}$

$= 1(1 - x) - x(1 - x^2) + 1(1 - x)$

$= (1 - x) - x(1 - x^2) + (1 - x)$

$= (2 - 2x) - (x - x^3)$

$= (2 - 2x - x + x^3)$

$= x^3 - 3x + 2$

Set $=0$: $(x-1)(x^2 + x - 2) = (x-1)(x-1)(x+2)$

Thus $x=1$ (double root), $x=-2$.

So (C) $x=1$ or $x=-2$.
